proposals: NHAI should publish each year the quantity and value of geotextiles used on National Highway projects, split between Indian MSME, other domestic and imported supply, so the “less than 30%” MSME share now known only from industry reporting becomes an official, trackable figure.

The Ministry of Textiles should publish annual export and import figures for each NTTM segment, including Agrotech and Geotech, using its own HSN-to-segment mapping, so segment trade positions like Agrotech’s $93 million surplus rest on an official series rather than a blog’s proxy mapping.

The Ministry of Jal Shakti should report the quantity of geotextiles and liners used in the canal-lining projects it funds, by domestic and imported source, so the agriculture-adjacent part of Geotech has its own import share instead of borrowing the highway figure as a proxy.

The Ministry of Textiles, with MoRTH, should publish a list of domestic manufacturers whose geotextiles have been tested against the specifications required on National Highway projects, so contractors can source from Indian MSMEs without defaulting to suppliers such as Huesker and TenCate.
